Team — forwarding FinClear's ask. Quick summary of what they want and what we should commit to in the DPA:

1) Timeline: They want 72 hours for confirmed incidents. Our current DPA language is 72 hours for "notification of confirmed breach affecting personal data" and 30 days for an initial investigatory update. We should stick to 72 hours for confirmed incidents but clarify what counts as "confirmed."

2) Scope: We can commit to providing: tenant IDs affected, event time window, relevant request/response logs (redacted where needed), and representative payload samples. We need legal sign-off on providing customer-identifying attributes — we'll default to pseudonymized samples unless FinClear signs an NDA addendum for targeted PII disclosure.

3) Evidence handoff: Operationally we can export logs and per-request traces (JSON/NDJSON), and produce archive exports of processed artifacts. We do not typically provide raw disk images unless judicially compelled. Timeline: logs/archives within 7 business days for prioritized requests; if forensics are needed we can negotiate expedited access and a provisional turnaround (T+14 business days) dependent on scope.

4) Subprocessors: We maintain responsibility for initial coordination with subprocessors we control. For subprocessors that are separate legal entities, we will act as liaison and collect evidence, but FinClear may need to execute a direct request if access is restricted by the subprocessor's contract. We should offer a cooperative clause: Redwood will attempt to obtain subprocessor artifacts within the same timelines but cannot guarantee those timelines where third-party controls apply.

Please propose exact wording for: (A) what "confirmed" means; (B) the notification cadence; (C) the language on subprocessor liaison vs direct request; (D) the evidence formats and SLA. Attach any templates or roster CSV.

Naomi

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is Redwood's proposed operational commitment (we can fold this into DPA language or an incident appendix). I'm copying our ops and legal leads for coordination.

Summary of commitments
- Notification: Redwood will provide initial notification of a confirmed incident affecting personal data within 72 hours of confirmation. "Confirmed" means (i) detection of unauthorized access or exfiltration or (ii) forensic indicators that reasonably indicate data exposure after triage by Redwood security AND corroborating telemetry from the impacted tenant(s). If additional investigation is required, Redwood will provide a written update within 30 calendar days and regular status updates every 7 calendar days until resolution.

- Notification contents: Initial notice will include affected tenant identifiers, incident time window, short summary of nature of the event, immediate mitigations taken, and contact points. On request, Redwood will provide representative request/response samples and redacted payloads to demonstrate impact; production of customer-identifying PII requires either (a) a targeted NDA addendum or (b) a lawful process (subpoena or court order).

- Evidence formats & SLAs: Redwood will deliver logs and trace exports in NDJSON/JSON formats. For prioritized evidence requests (escalated by security/legal), we will aim to deliver export bundles within 7 business days. For deeper forensic collections (full VM snapshots or disk images), Redwood will treat as a special request with a target of 14 business days subject to legal review and subprocessor constraints.

- Subprocessor coordination: Redwood will act as primary liaison to subprocessors we engage (we will request and aggregate evidence on FinClear's behalf). Where a subprocessor is contractually independent and denies direct access, Redwood will provide the subprocessor's contact and coordinate a joint request; timelines for subprocessor-provided artifacts are not guaranteed and will be communicated transparently.

- Contact roster & escalation: Primary SOC contact: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, +1-415-555-0132). Legal response lead: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com). Ops escalation: Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com). Attachment: redwood_liaison_roster.csv (contains names, roles, 24/7 escalation numbers).

Next steps
1) If FinClear is comfortable with the above, we'll draft a concise DPA appendix with the exact clause language and share a redline within 48 hours.
2) Please confirm whether you need a special NDA addendum to share sensitive samples; if so, we can provide a short form.
3) We will pre-seed the evidence-request template (attached) with the fields we will supply for a standard export.

If you want to set a short technical call to walk through formats and sample artifacts, Ben and Karthik are available this week.

Regards,
